newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam inflation continues downward spiral.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam inflation continues downward spiral.

text.p: Vietnam's consumer prices continued to fall this month, with annual inflation reaching a new low of 3.2 percent, the General Statistics Department said on Monday.
The figures showed prices fell 0.4 percent compared with July, marking the fourth consecutive month in which inflation levels have dropped.
Vietnam's statistics are routinely issued ahead of the end of the period which they measure.
Economists say the continued drop is a reflection of improved food distribution, a bumper rice harvest, and tighter credit limits.
World Bank officials have welcomed the low rate, but others have expressed concern that the continued fall could mean Vietnam's economy is coming off the boil.
State Bank governor Cao Si Kiem was quoted earlier this month by a local newspaper as saying that if inflation continued to drop there would be a negative impact on the economy.
An official of the central bank later said that credit limits on some 20 commercial banks were likely to be eased by the end of this year in order to help matters.

The 0.4. percent decline in prices was a smaller fall than the 0.7 percent drop in July. The statistics office data showed this was apparently due to exceptional price increases in areas of northern Vietnam which were badly hit by storms in July and earlier this month.
